account: Meitetsu EI Engineer, Toyota Systems and Toho Electric Industries developed an AI crossing image-analysis system. It was trialed from January 2023, with work on detection accuracy at night and in rain. ITmedia's 岡田有花 reported on 22 June 2026 that Odakyu Electric Railway would introduce an “AI踏切画像解析システム” from 24 June 2026. It covers four crossings on its Odawara Line. They are Minami-Shinjuku Nos. 2, 4 and 5 between Minami-Shinjuku and Sangubashi stations, and Mukogaoka-Yuen No. 9 between Mukogaoka-Yuen and Ikuta stations. The AI analyzes footage from the existing safety-confirmation cameras in real time. It identifies and tracks pedestrians, wheelchair users, bicycles and motorcycles. When it detects someone left inside after the barriers come down, it sends a signal through the signaling equipment. That signal applies the brakes of approaching trains and lights the crossing's special signal lamps to alert crews. Both are released automatically once the crossing is clear. Images are used only for hazard detection, and the system does not identify individuals. Analysis data are destroyed within a year. railf.jp carried the same announcement on 25 June 2026. Yomiuri reported on 19 September 2026 that trains made 17 emergency stops on detected anomalies in the system's first two months. The report does not say whether any stop averted an accident. It adds that the transport ministry now pays up to half the installation cost of such systems. Professor Ryo Takagi of Kogakuin University told the paper that such systems are very effective for accident prevention. He also warned that AI does not make crossings fully safe.

ai_role.statement: The AI detects people left inside the crossing and triggers the stop signal; the crew also sees a warning lamp. Yomiuri reports 17 stops, but it does not say how many came from AI detections, how many were real hazards or how often the system missed a person.

fields.account: Meitetsu EI Engineer, Toyota Systems and Toho Electric Industries developed an AI crossing image-analysis system. It was trialed from January 2023, with work on detection accuracy at night and in rain. ITmedia's 岡田有花 reported on 22 June 2026 that Odakyu Electric Railway would introduce an “AI踏切画像解析システム” from 24 June 2026. It covers four crossings on its Odawara Line. They are Minami-Shinjuku Nos. 2, 4 and 5 between Minami-Shinjuku and Sangubashi stations, and Mukogaoka-Yuen No. 9 between Mukogaoka-Yuen and Ikuta stations. The AI analyzes footage from the existing safety-confirmation cameras in real time. It identifies and tracks pedestrians, wheelchair users, bicycles and motorcycles. When it detects someone left inside after the barriers come down, it sends a signal through the signaling equipment. That signal applies the brakes of approaching trains and lights the crossing's special signal lamps to alert crews. Both are released automatically once the crossing is clear. Images are used only for hazard detection, and the system does not identify individuals. Analysis data are destroyed within a year. railf.jp carried the same announcement on 25 June 2026. Yomiuri reported on 19 September 2026 that trains made 17 emergency stops on detected anomalies in the system's first two months. The report does not say whether any stop averted an accident. It adds that the transport ministry now pays up to half the installation cost of such systems. Professor Ryo Takagi of Kogakuin University told the paper that such systems are very effective for accident prevention. He also warned that AI does not make crossings fully safe.
fields.summary: Odakyu's AI crossing image-analysis system reads existing crossing cameras and signals approaching trains to stop when someone is left inside; trains made 17 emergency stops in two months.
